scenes.ghost: Why is this a *problem* for the person quoted in the clip?
scenes.subtitle: The quote is authentic — {r|meaning the claim is taken at face value}, and that is where the discussion starts.

scenes.source: In Book Title, vol. 2, page 45, the author says:
scenes.body:
Whoever reads carefully will find that [[a claim on its own is not the same as its implication]], and that scholars have always drawn this distinction. [[The wording matters as much as the meaning.]]
Even so, the context of the passage decides how it is read.
scenes.subtitle: Now that we have the source in front of us, {g|notice the two highlighted lines}: the first separates the claim from its implication, and {g|the second ties it back to the wording}.

scenes.body: قال المؤلف: [[العبرة بالمعنى لا باللفظ]] وهذا أصل عظيم في الفهم، [[ولا يصح الاستدلال بالظاهر وحده]] دون النظر في السياق.
scenes.subtitle: The same point is made in the second source, {g|and it is worded even more directly}.
